subject: Reserved pool soft-guarantee & reservation drift — temporary uptime grace proposal
messages:
From: Miguel Santos <miguel.santos@pulseplay.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Lia Cheng <lia.cheng@pulseplay.ai>
Date: Sun, 10 Oct 2027 09:24:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated pool behavior and recent uptime/latency spikes

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the call last week. We're close to committing to a reserved GPU pool with Redwood but after pulling the Q3 telemetry I want to flag two items before legal signs the commitment:

- We've seen recurrent tail-latency spikes during our morning traffic ramp (07:00–10:00 PT) that correlate with other tenants doing heavier batching. That behavior is causing several customer-facing failed inference callbacks in our pipeline.
- On the reserved pool side we're worried about what we called "reservation drift" — transient reduction in effective reserved throughput when nodes move workloads (e.g., nightly batch jobs) cause queueing behavior to propagate.

Attached are a short SLO report and a small topology sketch so you can see our request in context.

Ask: can Redwood provide a temporary operational amendment that:
1) defines a short-term (6–8 week) soft-guarantee for dedicated pool uptime/latency during our business hours (06:00–18:00 PT),
2) specifies a queueing smoothing window and a bounded reservation-drift tolerance so our front-end can rely on a minimum throughput while we complete integration work?

We'd prefer defined fallback behaviors (e.g., routing to a pinned model variant or a warmed burst pool) rather than opaque failover. If possible, add a credit mechanism if the soft-guarantee is missed.

We are trying to align procurement/legal timelines for an October 20 signature. Can we please get a proposed amendment and an internal runbook note on how Redwood will observe and operate the smoothing window?

Thanks,
Miguel
Miguel Santos
VP Engineering, PulsePlay
Attachments: slo_report_q3.pdf (PDF, 2 pages); topology-diagram.png (PNG, 800x600)

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Miguel Santos <miguel.santos@pulseplay.ai>
Cc: Lia Cheng <lia.cheng@pulseplay.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 10 Oct 2027 12:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool behavior and recent uptime/latency spikes

Miguel — thanks for the level-setting and for sending the SLO extract. I reviewed the attachments and discussed initial options with SE.

Short answer: yes, we can offer a timeboxed operational amendment that provides a "soft-guarantee" during your business hours while we complete the integration. High-level proposal attached. Key points:

- Pilot window: 6 weeks active monitoring + 2 weeks ramp (we'll target Oct 25 start if you sign by Oct 20).
- Business-hours target: 99.5% availability on dedicated pool for 06:00–18:00 PT; tail-latency smoothing policy applied to concurrent queues.
- Reservation drift tolerance: allow up to 10% transient reduction in reserved effective capacity for periods under 15 minutes; during those moments we'll route best-effort traffic to a warmed burst pool or pinned variant as a fallback (configurable).
- Credits: formula in the draft — sliding scale capped at 15% of monthly reserved charge for the pilot period.
- Exclusions: planned maintenance windows and customer-initiated load tests.

Next steps: 1) I'll loop in Contracts and Customer Success to validate the credit language and craft the amendment; 2) confirm the runbook/observability hooks (we'll instrument resource-level metrics and provide a short alert digest).

Can we hop on a 30-min call tomorrow (Mon) at 10:30 PT to walk the proposal with your ops team? If that works, I'll send a calendar invite.

Regards,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
Attachment: proposed-amendment-draft.pdf

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 10 Oct 2027 15:45:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Dedicated pool behavior and recent uptime/latency spikes — internal notes

Folks — forwarding PulsePlay thread. TL;DR: customer asking for a 6–8 week soft-guarantee pilot (business hours), reservation-drift tolerance, queue-smoothing window, and credits. Attachments above.

Internal asks:
- Ben: please validate the technical approach. My proposed fallback is to route to a warmed burst pool (same model family, lower concurrency) for up to 5% of traffic during short drift events and to apply a queue-smoothing window of 6 minutes at the pool scheduler. Is that feasible without regressing other tenants?
- Lauren: we need a short amendment (pilot addendum) with explicit credit formula. Suggestion: credit X% of monthly reserved fee for each day where business-hours availability < target; sliding scale, capped at 15% for the pilot. Also add explicit maintenance exclusions and an opt-in for a second month extension.
- Naomi: CS will own runbook handoff and customer-facing observability digest. Can you confirm we can provide token-level latency breakdown (hourly) and a spike digest for PulsePlay?

Notes on negotiating levers: prefer an explicit timebox (6 weeks) and an opt-in extension. Keep the reservation-drift tolerance conservative (I recommend 10% / 15-minute window max). If legal pushes back on credits, offer a smaller credit and extended pilot (8 weeks) instead.

Attaching a quick credit calc I sketched that maps missed-hours to credit buckets. Please comment.

Grace
Attachment: credit-formula-sheet.csv

Date: Mon, 11 Oct 2027 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool behavior and recent uptime/latency spikes — proposed amendment and next steps

Hi Miguel / Lia — following our internal review and the call today, here's the agreed temporary amendment we can put in place immediately after signature:

Summary of binding pilot (proposal):
- Term: 6 weeks active pilot + 2-week ramp (start window: Oct 25–Nov 1 depending on your sign date).
- Business-hours target: 99.5% dedicated pool availability for 06:00–18:00 PT.
- Reservation-drift tolerance: tolerant of up to 10% transient reduction in effective reserved throughput for intervals under 15 minutes. During a drift event Redwood will: 1) attempt routing to a warmed burst pool or pinned model variant; 2) surface an incident digest to PulsePlay with token-level latency breakdown.
- Queueing smoothing: scheduler will apply a 6-minute smoothing window for inflight requests to avoid short-term preemption spikes.
- Credits: sliding daily credit table as discussed — credits accrue when business-hours availability falls below target; monthly cap 15% of reserved fee for the pilot. (See attached amendment for exact language.)
- Exclusions: planned maintenance declared with 48-hour notice, customer-driven stress tests, and force majeure.

Deliverables / Next steps:
1) I attached amendment-v1.docx. If the language looks good, please sign via the DocuSign link below so we can stand the pilot up by Oct 25.
2) Naomi will create the customer-facing runbook and daily digest sample; Ben will share the observability dashboard link and alert thresholds.
3) We will provision a warmed burst pool (one node) for the pilot and publish a short runbook that describes fallback routing.

DocuSign: https://docusign.net/Member/PowerFormSigning?PowerFormId=ABCD1234
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/4821

If anything in the amendment is a deal-breaker, we can discuss trading credit size vs. pilot length. Happy to take this over the finish line.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
